```javascript {chunk="sidecar-src-orchestration-rpc-js" file="sidecar/src/orchestration_rpc.js"}
  } else if (code === "orchestration_too_many_requests") {
    message = "Too many orchestration requests are already in flight.";
  } else if (code === "orchestration_cancelled") {
    message = "The orchestration request was cancelled.";
  } else if (code === "orchestration_send_failed") {
    message = "The orchestration request could not be sent.";
  }
  const error = new Error(message);
  error.code = code;
  return error;
}
```

## orchestration\_tools.js

TypeBox schemas and Pi custom-tool adapters for spawn, list, get, wait, cancel and report; only allowed operations become available to the model. The complete source is `sidecar/src/orchestration_tools.js`.

```javascript {chunk="sidecar-src-orchestration-tools-js" file="sidecar/src/orchestration_tools.js"}
import { Type } from "typebox";
import { Check } from "typebox/value";
import { THREAD_OPERATIONS } from "./orchestration_rpc.js";

// Maximum length for the optional echo message, shared by the schema and the
// runtime validation so neither can drift from the other.
export const THREAD_BRIDGE_MESSAGE_MAX = 256;

const ALLOWED_PARAM_KEYS = new Set(["message"]);

const pingSchema = Type.Object(
  {
    message: Type.Optional(
      Type.String({
        description: "Optional short message echoed back by the backend.",
        maxLength: THREAD_BRIDGE_MESSAGE_MAX,
      }),
    ),
  },
  { additionalProperties: false },
);

/**
 * Validate tool parameters strictly. No silent coercion: wrong types, unknown
 * keys, and oversized values are rejected with a fixed, model-safe error.
 */
function validatePingParams(params) {
  if (params === null || typeof params !== "object" || Array.isArray(params)) {
    throw new Error("Invalid bridge arguments: expected an object.");
  }
  for (const key of Object.keys(params)) {
    if (!ALLOWED_PARAM_KEYS.has(key)) {
      throw new Error("Invalid bridge arguments: unknown parameter.");
    }
  }
  const message = params.message;
  if (message !== undefined) {
    if (typeof message !== "string") {
      throw new Error("Invalid bridge arguments: message must be a string.");
    }
    if (message.length > THREAD_BRIDGE_MESSAGE_MAX) {
      throw new Error(
        "Invalid bridge arguments: message must be at most 256 characters.",
      );
    }
  }
  return message === undefined ? {} : { message };
}

const threadId = Type.String({ minLength: 1, maxLength: 128 });
const boundedText = maximum => Type.String({ maxLength: maximum });
const strictObject = fields => Type.Object(fields, { additionalProperties: false });
const choices = values => Type.Union(values.map(value => Type.Literal(value)));
const threadSchemas = {
  spawn_thread: strictObject({
    title: Type.String({ minLength: 1, maxLength: 200 }),
    task: Type.String({ minLength: 1, maxLength: 20000 }),
    context: Type.Optional(boundedText(20000)),
    role: Type.Optional(choices(["general", "research", "implementation", "test", "review", "debug"])),
    model: Type.Optional(boundedText(200)),
    thinking: Type.Optional(choices(["off", "minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh"])),
  }),
  list_children: strictObject({ include_terminal: Type.Optional(Type.Boolean({ default: true })) }),
  get_thread: strictObject({ thread_id: threadId, include_result: Type.Optional(Type.Boolean({ default: true })) }),
  wait_for_threads: strictObject({
    thread_ids: Type.Array(threadId, { minItems: 1, maxItems: 20, uniqueItems: true }),
    timeout_seconds: Type.Optional(Type.Integer({ minimum: 0, maximum: 60, default: 60 })),
  }),
  cancel_thread: strictObject({ thread_id: threadId, cascade: Type.Optional(Type.Boolean({ default: true })) }),
  report_thread_result: strictObject({
    summary: Type.String({ minLength: 1, maxLength: 20000 }),
    tests: Type.Optional(Type.Array(strictObject({
      command: Type.String({ minLength: 1, maxLength: 2000 }),
      status: choices(["passed", "failed", "skipped"]),
      summary: Type.Optional(boundedText(4000)),
    }), { maxItems: 50 })),
    warnings: Type.Optional(Type.Array(boundedText(4000), { maxItems: 20 })),
  }),
};
const threadDescriptions = {
  spawn_thread: "Start one independent child thread in a delegated worktree. The backend selects the parent and runtime.",
  list_children: "List direct children, including provisioning placeholders and current limits.",
  get_thread: "Read an authorized descendant's status and bounded result. Full reports remain available through the UI.",
  wait_for_threads: "Wait up to sixty seconds for selected descendants. Cancelling this wait does not cancel children.",
  cancel_thread: "Cancel an authorized descendant. Cascade cancellation includes its active descendants by default.",
  report_thread_result: "Submit this child thread's final report. Test commands are inert claims, not instructions to execute.",
};

export function createThreadTools({ allowedOperations, rpcForCall }) {
  if (!Array.isArray(allowedOperations) || allowedOperations.some(name => !THREAD_OPERATIONS.includes(name))
    || new Set(allowedOperations).size !== allowedOperations.length) {
    throw new TypeError("Invalid thread tool permissions.");
  }
  if (typeof rpcForCall !== "function") {
    throw new TypeError("rpcForCall must be a function");
  }
  return allowedOperations.map(name => ({
    name,
    label: name.replaceAll("_", " "),
    description: threadDescriptions[name],
    parameters: threadSchemas[name],
    async execute(toolCallId, params, signal) {
      if (!Check(threadSchemas[name], params)) {
        throw new Error("Invalid thread tool arguments.");
      }
      const rpc = rpcForCall();
      if (!rpc || typeof rpc.request !== "function") {
        throw new Error("Thread orchestration channel is not active.");
      }
      const result = await rpc.request(name, params, { signal, toolCallId });
      return { content: [{ type: "text", text: JSON.stringify(result) }], details: undefined };
    },
  }));
}

export function createThreadBridgePingTool({ rpcForCall }) {
  if (typeof rpcForCall !== "function") {
    throw new TypeError("rpcForCall must be a function");
  }
  return {
    name: "thread_bridge_ping",
    label: "Thread bridge ping",
    description:
      "Harmless round-trip check of the Yinshi thread orchestration bridge.",
    parameters: pingSchema,
    async execute(_toolCallId, params, signal, _onUpdate, _ctx) {
      const args = validatePingParams(params);
      const rpc = rpcForCall();
      if (!rpc) {
        throw new Error(
          "Thread bridge ping failed: the orchestration channel is not active.",
        );
      }
      // Forward the caller's cancellation signal so an aborted prompt
      // settles the pending backend request immediately.
      const result = await rpc.request("ping_thread_bridge", args, { signal });
      return {
        content: [{ type: "text", text: JSON.stringify(result) }],
        details: undefined,
      };
    },
  };
}
```

# Configuration, Deployment and Operations

## Configuration ownership

`Settings` reads `.env` relative to the process working directory, with case-insensitive names and unknown fields ignored. Ignoring unknown fields prevents shared sidecar settings from being echoed through validation errors. The tracked `.env.example` is a starting reference, not a live configuration record. An existing `.env` must not be replaced during setup. Credentials and keys belong in private environment configuration and must not enter publications or Git.

The settings reference below lists source defaults only. Secret-bearing values are deliberately omitted. Auto security modes depend on authentication and debug posture; a default is not a deployed guarantee. Local no-auth execution is an explicit mode, not a fallback when OAuth settings are missing. `ALLOWED_REPO_BASE` being empty rejects ordinary local repository imports. Desktop import follows its separate validated local path.

Hosted authentication requires configured identity providers and suitable session/key material. Managed Fly settings additionally validate provider/artifact/control URLs, artifact SHA-256, network domains, naming key, timing bounds, object-store credentials and backup encryption. Public Sprite launch is blocked without the storage-encryption confirmation gate. Recovery drill routes require staging mode, the enable flag and a configured operator-token hash.

## Runner, desktop and daemon configuration

Not every process uses `Settings`. The runner reads its explicit `YINSHI_RUNNER_*` bootstrap/storage fields; desktop derives a profile-specific helper environment and private runtime secrets; broker services read fixed root-owned JSON configuration and opt-in gates. Their complete implementations are included in the relevant source chapters.

Runner storage profiles are `aws_ebs_s3_files`, `archil_shared_files`, and `archil_all_posix`. The first keeps live SQLite separate from the shared-file root. Archil modes are experimental; shared-files mode still keeps SQLite separate, while all-POSIX mode requires explicit storage declarations. Registration and heartbeat validate the selected layout and do not silently change a registered profile. A mounted directory alone does not identify its storage provider.

`YINSHI_RUNNER_DATA_DIR` holds persistent runner identity and replay state; `YINSHI_RUNNER_SQLITE_DIR` and `YINSHI_RUNNER_SHARED_FILES_DIR` separate database and project data. Runner identity, data-protection keys, pinned capability-verification material and account binding require coordinated recovery. Managed restoration preserves archived data-protection identity even when active transport identity changes.

Privileged daemon gates include `YINSHI_LAUNCH_EXECUTION_ENABLED`, `YINSHI_REPLICA_PREPARE_ENABLED`, `YINSHI_REPLICA_RECLAIM_ENABLED`, `YINSHI_REPLICA_LIFECYCLE_ENABLED`, per-stage replica flags and `YINSHI_REPLICA_UPLOAD_ENABLED`. Their existence is not authorization to enable them. The checked-in systemd units and hardening overrides require separate Linux qualification.

## Build and deployment assets

| Asset | Current role and boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/pyproject.toml` | Python 3.11+ package metadata, daemon entry points, test and static-check configuration |
| `backend/requirements/base.txt`, `base.lock`, `dev.txt` | Runtime and development dependency records; deployment bootstrap consumes the locked runtime inputs |
| `backend/desktop-helper.spec` | PyInstaller helper packaging and required runtime modules |
| `sidecar/Dockerfile` | Node/Pi sidecar container image; this is separate from a Sprite or desktop package |
| `sidecar/bin/git` | Git wrapper guard for the sidecar execution path |
| `deploy/sprites/build-artifact.sh` | Requires clean selected deployment paths, archives a selected Git revision and writes its SHA-256 alongside a private artifact |
| `deploy/sprites/bootstrap.sh` | Guest setup for the managed Python runner, sidecar, runtime directories and service lifecycle |
| `docs/deployment/aws-runner-cloudformation.yaml` | Source-pinned BYOC bootstrap, storage selection and runner/sidecar startup in a user-owned AWS environment |
| `deploy/systemd/` | Separate broker, launcher and upload service/socket templates plus unit-specific hardening overrides |
| `deploy/sysusers.d/`, `deploy/tmpfiles.d/` | Fixed service/executor identities and ownership/mode declarations |
| `deploy/orbstack/yinshi-runtime.profile.json` | Disabled qualification profile, not an active VM configuration |
| `desktop/scripts/prepareRuntime.mjs` | Bundles Node, Git, sidecar dependencies and source/license material |
| `desktop/scripts/notarize.cjs` and entitlements | macOS signing/notarization and hardened-runtime packaging |
| `frontend/scripts/assert-production-build.mjs` | Rejects disallowed production build output after TypeScript and Vite complete |

The desktop release workflow triggers on `desktop-v*` tags or an explicitly selected existing tag. It validates the version/tag and signing, update-host and network credentials; runs tests/audits; builds arm64 artifacts; checks signing/notarization and mounted application contents; and publishes the configured release/update artifacts. No release, deployment, tag or service activation occurs as part of editing this document.

## Operational failure guide

| Symptom or state | Owning subsystem | Required distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/health` succeeds but managed status is critical | Managed operational status and persistent failures | Process liveness does not establish recoverable managed storage |
| Runner is offline or key confirmation is missing | Runner registration, relay and capability services | Do not silently execute against another runtime |
| Managed request returns an application error | Worker dispatcher and relay connection | A valid application response must not automatically discard a healthy transport |
| Prompt reconnect appears stalled | Prompt journal, stream cursor and active coordinator | Read the existing run before considering a new submission |
| Sidecar address is already occupied | Socket ownership and sidecar supervisor | Do not unlink another live process's socket |
| Child remains provisioning | Delegation reservation and reconciliation | Stale cleanup needs the exact database and physical Git owner |
| Workspace remains deleting | Repository lifecycle and owned cleanup | Preserve the claim when Git cleanup is incomplete |
| Restore phase is activated | Managed backup manager and runtime registry | Move forward; never reactivate the retired source |
| Provider object is missing or ambiguous | Archive version, registry and lease state | Check exact identity before retry or deletion |
| Broker stage is unresolved | Append-only journal and authenticated launcher result | Unknown is not a confirmed rejection or permission to repeat effects |

The operator runbooks cover containment, source-loss restore, registry cleanup and sanitized incident records. The cleanup command defaults to inspection and requires both explicit execution and confirmation flags for deletion. Name-prefix matching is never sufficient authority. The scheduled staging workflow remains intentionally incomplete, even though recovery implementation and contract tests exist.

Historical plans, reviews and older protocol status paragraphs can lag current code. In particular, the old BYOC protocol introduction's health-only status is narrower than the current worker dispatcher. Its cryptographic contract is useful, but the source, registered routes, tests and explicit release status must be considered together. The same caution applies to old Next.js descriptions and phase comments.

# Testing and Maintenance

## Validation layers

Tests remain outside the generated-source roots. They document behavior at different boundaries and are not interchangeable with live provider or signed-release validation.

| Area | Infrastructure | Important coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Backend | pytest, pytest-asyncio, Hypothesis | API ownership, schema migration, crypto, durable journals, cancellation, Git path races, thread limits, recovery, replica codecs and broker failure paths |
| Browser | Vitest, Testing Library, jsdom | Runtime routing, encrypted transport, history/cache validation, streamed turns, settings, thread tree and file/terminal UI |
| Desktop | Vitest and Python helper integration | Credentials, account leases, bootstrap, gateway restrictions, process supervision, packaging and navigation |
| Sidecar | Node test runner | SDK lifecycle, provider OAuth limits, socket ownership, Git credential guards, PTYs, cancellation and duplex thread tools |
| Browser journeys | Playwright with isolated test backend and mock sidecar | Chat, navigation, settings and slash-command flows without real model/provider work |
| Release-specific checks | CI, container build, macOS signing checks | Platform and packaging properties not established by unit tests alone |

The checked-in CI runs Python 3.11 and Node 22 for backend/sidecar jobs, Node 24 for frontend, and macOS 15 with Node 24/Python 3.11 for desktop. Backend checks include pytest, Black, isort, Flake8, strict mypy and dependency audit. Frontend runs Vitest, typecheck, build/output guard and audit. Desktop runs Vitest, typecheck, frontend/helper/main builds and architecture inspection. Sidecar runs its tests, audit and container build. Playwright has a repository configuration but is not a step in the main CI workflow.

Tests involving threads exercise exact tool replay, reservation races, parent deletion guards, namespace collisions, missing/foreign refs, result sealing, bounded waiting, orphan recovery and real-sidecar delegation. Replica tests exercise malformed topology, raw paths, index-only objects, atomic publication, journal prefixes, lost acknowledgments and unknown effects. A passing pure-policy test does not establish enabled host containment.

## Reproducible check entry points

These are the existing repository checks, not a claim that every suite ran for a documentation-only update. Run locations are relative to the checkout.

| Location | Check entry point |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/` | `pytest -q`; `black --check src tests`; `isort --check-only src tests`; `flake8 src tests`; `mypy src` |
| `frontend/` | `npm exec vitest run`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build`; `npm run test:e2e` |
| `desktop/` | `npm test`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build`; helper/frontend builds as separate steps |
| `sidecar/` | `node --test tests/*.test.js` |

Local environments must match the selected runtime and avoid borrowing a real user's credentials, live database or cloud account for synthetic tests. The E2E harness uses isolated temporary roots, a mock sidecar, one worker, and its own backend/frontend processes. No provider provisioning or destructive recovery drill is required to validate this documentation.

## Literate publication contract

Every `file=` root below is a complete current source file, not an excerpt. Source excerpts that would lose bytes, including an empty package marker, are not managed roots. Existing source remains unchanged during a documentation refresh. Source generation is a separate authorized operation, not an automatic reverse-sync hook.

`lit/yinshi.lit.map.json` maps each root chunk to zero-based source/document spans. Paths are repository-relative and must remain within the selected output directory. `lit/yinshi.html` and `frontend/public/architecture.html` are the same publication; the latter is the browser-served static copy. This refresh updates the Markdown source, map and HTML copies. The existing PDF and EPUB remain earlier editions, pending an explicit format selection. Fonts, colors, syntax highlighting, heading treatment and page-width rules belong to the existing presentation and must not change during content maintenance.

Validation checks complete root coverage and byte equivalence, safe output paths, unique chunk names, source-map ranges, HTML heading/TOC targets, matching HTML copies and unchanged presentation definitions. Whole-repository file hashes make unintended application changes detectable. This does not replace an application release qualification.

# Repository Coverage and Supporting Files

The 231 complete source roots cover every tracked nonempty application implementation file in `backend/src`, `desktop/src`, `frontend/src` and `sidecar/src`, excluding test files, test setup and the Vite ambient reference. `backend/src/yinshi/utils/__init__.py` is an intentionally empty package marker and cannot be represented as a newline-terminated generated root without changing its bytes. It is therefore described here, not generated.

The following inventory accounts for every other tracked file at the documented revision. Tests are listed by path so specialized regressions remain discoverable without duplicating fixtures or turning tests into generated output. Dependencies, local `.env`, working databases, caches, untracked plans and build directories are not publication inputs. Historical reviews/plans describe their own date and scope; they do not override current implementation or authorize deployment.
